Widgets

A cmd widget is a small package: React made of cmd's own elements, reading your agents, terminals and windows live. It draws like a built-in window, asks before it reaches anything, and is tested without a browser.

Make one

cmd widget new my-widget       # a package with a widget, its test, its story, CLAUDE.md
cd my-widget
cmd widget dev                 # on the board, its console here; saves reload it
npm test                       # or cmd widget test
cmd widget check               # package.json, permissions, types
cmd widget preview . --themes all --sizes all

Or ask Magic for one: it writes the same kind of package. Agents working in a package read its CLAUDE.md and this reference, which cmd widget new links at node_modules/@cmd/widget-api/README.md.

cmd · cmd.workspace · cmd.agents · cmd.terminals · cmd.windows · cmd.events · cmd.git · cmd.actions · cmd.notify · cmd.net · cmd.ai · cmd.run · cmd.config · cmd.state · cmd.env · cmd.fmt · Hooks · Elements

API 1, minor 1. Everything here is in API 1 for good; what came after 1.0 says @since 1.x, and a widget that also runs on an older cmd checks cmd.env.has(verb) first.

cmd

cmd, as a widget sees it. Reads run at once within the widget's grant; acts (1.1) ask the person (docs/55), only right after they pressed something in the widget, and only in its own workspace. Every method is async and rejects with an ApiCallError when the grant lacks what it needs (error.permission names it) or the person says no (code: "denied").

cmd.net

The network, through the core: the widget process has none of its own.

VerbSincePermissionWhat
cmd.net.fetch(url: string, init?: ApiFetchInit | undefined): Promise<ApiFetchResponse>1.0net: [<host>]Fetches url through the core, which checks its host against the widget's net grant (net: ["api.github.com"]). init.auth names a secret config field: the core attaches its value, only to the host that field is bound to, and the widget never sees it. The body comes back as text, clipped past the core's limit.

cmd.run

Programs, through the core: cmd.run("gh", ["run", "list"]). Needs run: [<program>].

VerbSincePermissionWhat
cmd.run(program: string, args?: string[] | undefined, opts?: ApiRunOptions | undefined): Promise<ApiRunResult>1.1run: [<program>]Runs a program the widget declares in run (run: ["gh"]) through the core, never a shell: args reach it as they are. Only read-only commands run (the same rules as Magic's: gh run list yes, gh run rerun or git -c alias.x=… no; a refusal says why). At most 10 s by default (timeoutMs, up to 30 s), 64 KB of stdout and 16 KB of stderr (more is cut, clipped), 2 at once and 30 a minute; tokens in the output are blanked. Its folder is the workspace's unless cwd names another in it or in read.
cmd.run.exec(program: string, args?: string[] | undefined, opts?: ApiRunOptions | undefined): Promise<ApiRunResult>1.1run: [<program>]The same as calling cmd.run: the verb's name on the wire.

Hooks

The reads as subscriptions: each gets the current value at once and every change after, until its component unmounts.

HookSinceWhat
useActions(): ApiAction[]1.0The workspace's Actions (docs/36), live.
useAgents(query?: ApiScopeQuery): ApiAgent[]1.0The agents of this workspace (or every workspace with { scope: "all" }), live: a row updates when an agent's state, name or line changes. Empty until they arrive. Needs workspace: ["read"] (["all"] for every workspace).
useCompletion(request: ApiCompletionRequest | null): CompletionState1.0Asks the person's AI once per distinct request (a new prompt asks again; null asks nothing): cmd.ai.complete as a hook. Needs ai: ["complete"].
useConfig<T extends ConfigShape<T> = Record<string, WireValue>>() => T1.0This window's config values (from package.json's config fields, as the person set them, else their defaults), live, typed by cmd-env.d.ts. Secret fields are never here: a widget never holds a secret (cmd.net.fetch's auth names one).
useData<T>(fn: (): Promise<T>, opts?: { every?: number | undefined; }) => DataState<T>1.0The outside world on a timer: runs fn (a cmd.net.fetch) now and every every seconds (default 60), keeps the last good data through failures and says how fresh it is. A run that throws keeps the old data with stale and error set.
useEnv(): WidgetEnv1.0Where the widget runs: cmd's version, the API served, the theme, the size class and the placement (board or sidebar), live.
useEvents(query?: ApiEventQuery): ApiEvent[]1.0Events from the log matching query, newest last: the query's result first, then each new one as it happens; at most query.limit (default 200) are kept. Needs events: [<class>] for each class of events it reads.
useGit(): ApiGitStatus | null1.0The workspace's git status (branch, ahead/behind, changed files), live; null outside a repository.
useNow(every?: number): number1.0The time now, re-rendering every every ms (default 1000): for ages that move.
useStoredState<T extends WireValue>(key: string, initial: T): [T, (next: T | ((prev: T) => T)) => void]1.0A value kept by the core for this window across reloads and restarts, like useState. The first render already has the stored value.
useTerminals(query?: ApiScopeQuery): ApiTerminal[]1.0The terminals of this workspace (or all), live.
useWindows(query?: ApiScopeQuery): ApiWindow[]1.0The windows of this workspace (or all), live, with which is selected.
useWorkspace(): ApiWorkspace | null1.0The widget's workspace (id, name, folder, branch), live; null until it arrives. Needs workspace: ["read"].

defineWidget<Config extends ConfigShape<Config> = Record<string, WireValue>>(render: (props: { config: Config; }) => ReactNode) => Widget: Declares a widget: render is its view, called with this window's config (live). The module's default export is what cmd runs; a plain component works too. export default defineWidget<{ repo: string }>(({ config }) => <Text>{config.repo}</Text>);

Elements

The app draws each with its kit; a tree can name nothing else. Handlers (onClick, a menu entry's run) are functions in the widget and ids on the wire.

Window

The widget's window, around everything: the title bar (icon and name from the manifest), its status line and menus. Optional; a widget without one gets the bare title bar.

PropTypeWhat
statusstring | nullThe title bar's status line ("2 waiting for you · 1 working"); null for none.
menuMenuEntry[]The title menu (a scope switch: This Workspace / All Workspaces).
actionsMenuEntry[]Entries added to the window's context menu.
childrenReactNodeThe window's content: a View.
